summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, recent CABG and mitral valve replacement, and end-stage renal disease was admitted from rehab due to two episodes of brown vomiting, initially concerning for GI bleeding. She denied pain, nausea, or further vomiting. Labs showed stable hemoglobin and a negative stool test. Elevated troponin was attributed to chronic kidney disease, not acute coronary syndrome. A chest X-ray showed persistent pulmonary edema and pleural effusions. GI consultation found no need for endoscopy, suspecting tube-related irritation. She underwent scheduled hemodialysis, was started on metoprolol post-CABG, and given ondansetron for nausea. She remained stable, with no recurrent vomiting, and was discharged back to rehab with updated medications and follow-up plans.
